tagline: A short road loop through farmsteads and a stone mill’s changing uses.
intro: Boone Creek Scenic Byway makes an 8.6-mile circuit using KY 418, Grimes Mill Road and McCalls Mill Road in Fayette and Clark counties. Its setting includes Boone Creek’s rural historic district, with historic farmsteads and the Grimes House and Mill Complex. The Kentucky Transportation Cabinet records the scenic designation on May 24, 1995.

The roads link places whose uses changed as older industries disappeared. At Athens, fires had destroyed the manufacturing buildings by 1860. Grimes Mill worked until 1927, then became the Iroquois Hunt’s headquarters after its purchase the following year. The mill’s quarried-stone walls are three and a half feet thick.

Begin on KY 418 southeast of its junction with KY 1973, continuing into Clark County to Grimes Mill Road. Follow Grimes Mill Road back into Fayette County, where the mill’s stone springhouse stands beside the road. McCalls Mill Road completes the return to KY 418.

moments.title: Athens
moments.text: Athens’ surviving village buildings tell only part of the story: fire removed much of its commercial and industrial center. The community once had a woolen factory and works making bagging and rope; by 1860, all its manufacturing buildings had burned. Among the surviving buildings, the Dr. Parker House combines log and frame construction, while the Marshall Tavern is brick. The older buildings have mostly become homes, leaving few in commercial use. The Aubrey Inn stands at the corner of Main and Cleveland Road; another log building beside the Parker House is covered in clapboards.

moments.title: Boone Creek Rural Historic District
moments.text: The historic landscape here extends beyond any single mill or farmhouse. Boone Creek Rural Historic District spans western Clark and eastern Fayette counties and includes the Grimes complex, Cleveland-Rogers House and James Pettit’s Mill. Its National Register listing in 1994 covered 4,060 acres, with 88 contributing buildings, 55 structures and 25 sites. The nomination describes farmsteads whose arrangement responds to the landforms, contrasting that pattern with the more regular terrain and intensive horse-farm development elsewhere in rural Fayette County. The nomination also notes newer barns and houses that follow traditional choices of building sites and scale.

moments.title: Grimes Mill
moments.text: Grimes Mill’s walls are three and a half feet thick, built of quarried stone around a hand-hewn wooden support system. The mill remained in use until 1927. The following year, the Iroquois Hunt bought it for a permanent headquarters. The hunt took its name from Iroquois, the first American-bred horse to win the Epsom Derby, in 1881. Across Grimes Mill Road, the stone springhouse faces the roadway, with a stone doorway and an earthen mound. The wider complex includes the Grimes family home, a cemetery, and foundations left by a flax house and distillery.
moments.notice: The stone springhouse stands across the road from the mill and faces Grimes Mill Road.
